tests.title: GET /api/watchlist/ lists the user's movies in the order added
Adding saves the entry; a duplicate gets 400
Removing deletes the entry; a missing one gets 404
The status check returns true or false
Add: missing, malformed and unknown movie ids
Each user has their own watchlist
Failed requests count toward the limit
Reading the watchlist isn't rate limited

bugs.why: getWatchlist looks the entries up by movie id (with the user's id), so the list is always empty
bugs.fix: Use watchlistRepository.findByUserIdOrderByCreatedAtAscIdAsc(userId): the user's entries in the order they were added.

bugs.why: addToWatchlist builds a Watchlist entry but never saves it, and never checks for duplicates
bugs.fix: Answer 400 "Movie already in watchlist" when existsByUserIdAndMovieId(...), otherwise watchlistRepository.save(...). The unique constraint and the DataIntegrityViolationException branch are only a safety net.

bugs.why: removeFromWatchlist looks the entry up but never deletes it, and never answers 404
bugs.fix: long deleted = watchlistRepository.deleteByUserIdAndMovieId(userId, movieId), then 404 "Movie not found in watchlist" when it's 0.

bugs.why: checkWatchlistStatus returns the list of entries instead of true / false
bugs.fix: Use existsByUserIdAndMovieId(...), which returns a boolean.

bugs.why: the limiter's path pattern for remove has a trailing slash, so POST /api/watchlist/remove isn't limited (Spring 6 doesn't match trailing slashes)
bugs.fix: Register the interceptor for "/api/watchlist/remove", without the slash.

bugs.why: the rate limiter keeps the expired timestamps (>= instead of <), so recent requests are never counted and nobody is limited
bugs.fix: Keep the timestamps with now - stamp < WINDOW_MS.
